result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService, refreshOAuthTokens may return a raw fetch Response (when credential sharing is enabled and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set), but the caller does `const token = res?.data;` then `token.access_token`, which throws since a fetch Response has no `.data`. The diff indeed introduces refreshOAuthTokens returning `response` from `fetch` directly while the google path previously destructured `{ res }` from myGoogleAuth.refreshToken whose res had `.data`.

judged_text: With credential sharing enabled, Google refresh crashes: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response but caller reads res?.data, causing token.access_token to throw

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a native `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set. A `Response` does not have `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime under credential sharing.
